palette.notes: Live camera footage of a physical perler-bead piece, so the measured palette (1) is meaningless. The beads themselves use a teal-to-navy ramp for hair and boots with near-black shadows and pale cyan highlights.

lighting: Real room light on the beads; inside the artwork the shading is baked into bead colours, light top-left, dark navy on the lower edges.
silhouette: A full-body anime character (Miku) in a big diagonal leap pose with streaming twin tails and wings, readable from across the room once the camera pulls back.

motion.timing: Measured 30 drawings/s on 1s: this is continuous camera footage, not frame-by-frame animation. All movement is the camera pulling back; the art itself is still.

texture: Every pixel is a round bead with a hole, on a pink gingham pegboard; the physical grid is the texture.
camera: Starts in an extreme close-up of tweezers placing one bead on a boot, then a continuous zoom-out that reveals legs, then the whole figure on the board.

acting.enters: Only a boot tip and the tweezers are visible; the character is hidden by the framing.
acting.acts: No acting; the reveal does the work: the frame keeps widening until the full pose lands.
acting.depth: Scale is the whole trick: one bead fills the frame at first, then the full character is small in a wider shot.

techniques: detail-first reveal: open on one placed pixel, pull back to the full image
POV text hook stays on screen the whole time
physical pixels (beads) make the grid itself the selling point
teal-to-navy ramp with near-black shadow beads
feel: one bead in close-up + continuous pull-back to the full pose = satisfying 8-second payoff
for_fred: Open a reel on an extreme close-up of one part of Fred (an eye, one fin pixel) and pull back to reveal him small in the full scene; the reveal is the hook. Not character animation, so take only the staging.
